perspective:
**Ethan’s available information:**

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my close friend from middle school; he is a doctor. We have long relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- I noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. I invited him to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation/rejuvenation, telling him his health matters and it might give him a new perspective. Gary said he appreciated my concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected his overworking was about more than professional obligations. I told him we had been friends since middle school, he could tell me anything, and I was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden me.
- Gary then opened up to me about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. I felt relief and empathy. I offered to help him prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities, saying he didn’t have to do everything himself. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I checked in regularly with Gary about his progress and remaining challenges. I saw him making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and told him I was proud and available whenever he needed to talk. Gary told me things were better, he was not as overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, I saw Gary was capable of managing on his own. I felt satisfied and happy for him, decided to step back, and told him I’m always just a call away and that he’s got this. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and said he felt more in control.
